candidate.answerReason: The only two-digit factor pair is 77 and 85. Their product is 6545 and their sum is 162, matching A.

methods.label: Narrow the factor search
methods.explanation:
The two-digit condition sharply limits the search. Each factor is at most \(99\), so neither can be \(66\) or smaller, because
\[
66\cdot99=6534<6545.
\]
Thus both factors must lie between \(67\) and \(99\).

Since \(6545\) is odd, both factors are odd. Multiplying two odd units digits from \(1,3,7,9\) never gives a units digit of \(5\), so at least one factor must end in \(5\). In our range, that factor can only be \(75\), \(85\), or \(95\). Check these three possibilities:
\[
\begin{aligned}
6545&=75\cdot87+20,\\
6545&=85\cdot77,\\
6545&=95\cdot68+85.
\end{aligned}
\]
The nonzero remainders eliminate \(75\) and \(95\). Therefore the pair is \(85\) and \(77\), both of which are two-digit numbers. Their sum is
\[
85+77=\boxed{162},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses whole-number bounds, odd and even numbers, units digits, and three arithmetic checks. It needs no formal congruences or prime-factorization machinery.
